def: A written trace of intermediate reasoning steps produced before an answer, which gives later tokens more serial computation to draw on.
A pattern that alternates a model's reasoning (thought), a tool request (action) and the real tool output (observation) in a loop.
The real result of a tool call, appended to the transcript so the model can ground its next thought.
An agent design in which a planner first writes an explicit list of steps and an executor then carries them out, with a bounded replan on failure.
The model call that turns a goal into an explicit list of steps before any step is executed.
Evaluating an attempt, turning the verdict into feedback and trying again, which helps most when the feedback comes from tests or validators rather than the model's own opinion.
Feedback produced by something outside the model, such as test results, schema validators or retrieval checks, rather than by its self-assessment.
A model trained, typically with reinforcement learning on checkable outcomes, to produce a long internal chain of thought before its final reply.
A cap on how many tokens a model may spend reasoning before it answers, trading answer quality against cost and latency.
Reasoning by the model between tool calls within one turn, so it can read each tool result before deciding the next action.
